verses.zh: （可拉后裔的诗歌，就是以斯拉人希幔的训诲诗，交与伶长。调用麻哈拉利暗俄。）耶和华―拯救我的　神啊，我昼夜在你面前呼吁。
verses.en: A song, a psalm written by the Korahites, for the music director, according to the machalath-leannoth style;[NOTE:1] a well-written song[NOTE:2] by Heman the Ezrahite.O Lord God who delivers me,[NOTE:3] by day I cry outand at night I pray before you.[NOTE:4]
notes: Psalm 88. The psalmist cries out in pain to the Lord, begging him for relief from his intense and constant suffering. The psalmist regards God as the ultimate cause of his distress, but nevertheless clings to God in hope.

The Hebrew phrase מָחֲלַת לְעַנּוֹת (makhalat leʿannot) may mean “illness to afflict.” Perhaps it refers to a particular style of music, a tune title, or a musical instrument. The term מָחֲלַת also appears in the superscription of Ps 53.

The meaning of the Hebrew term מַשְׂכִּיל (maskil) is uncertain. The word is derived from a verb meaning “to be prudent; to be wise.” Various options are: “a contemplative song,” “a song imparting moral wisdom,” or “a skillful [i.e., well-written] song.” The term occurs in the superscriptions of Pss 32, 42, 44, 45, 52-55, 74, 78, 88, 89, and 142, as well as in Ps 47:7.

Heb “O Lord God of my deliverance.” In light of the content of the psalm, this reference to God as the one who delivers seems overly positive. For this reason some assume dittography of the י (yod) and emend the text from אֱלֹהֵי יְשׁוּעָתִי (ʾelohe yeshuʿati) to אֱלֹהַי שִׁוַּעְתִּי (ʾelohay shivvaʿtiy, “[O Lord] my God, I cry out”). See v. 13.

verses.zh: 愿我的祷告达到你面前；求你侧耳听我的呼求！
verses.en: Listen to my prayer.[NOTE:1] Pay attention[NOTE:2] to my cry for help.
notes: Heb “[by] day I cry out, in the night before you.”
Heb “may my prayer come before you.” The prefixed verbal form is understood as a jussive, indicating the psalmist’s desire or prayer.

verses.zh: 因为我心里满了患难；我的性命临近阴间。
verses.en: For my life[NOTE:1] is filled with troubles,and I am ready to enter Sheol.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “turn your ear.”
Or “my soul.”

verses.zh: 我算和下坑的人同列，如同无力（或译：没有帮助）的人一样。
verses.en: They treat me like[NOTE:1] those who descend into the grave.[NOTE:2] I am like a helpless man,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and my life approaches Sheol.”
Heb “I am considered with.”
Heb “the pit.” The noun בּוֹר (bor, “pit,” “cistern”) is sometimes used of the grave and/or the realm of the dead.

verses.zh: 我被丢在死人中，好像被杀的人躺在坟墓里。他们是你不再记念的，与你隔绝了。
verses.en: adrift[NOTE:1] among the dead,like corpses lying in the gravewhom you remember no moreand who are cut off from your power.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I am like a man [for whom] there is no help.”
Heb “set free.”

verses.zh: 你把我放在极深的坑里，在黑暗地方，在深处。
verses.en: You place me in the lowest regions of the Pit,[NOTE:1] in the dark places, in the watery depths.
notes: Heb “from your hand.”

verses.zh: 你的忿怒重压我身；你用一切的波浪困住我。（细拉）
verses.en: Your anger bears down on me,and you overwhelm me with all your waves. (Selah)

verses.zh: 你把我所认识的隔在远处，使我为他们所憎恶；我被拘困，不得出来。
verses.en: You cause those who know me to keep their distance;you make me an appalling sight to them.I am trapped and cannot get free.[NOTE:1]
notes: The noun בּוֹר (bor, “pit,” “cistern”) is sometimes used of the grave and/or the realm of the dead. See v. 4.

verses.zh: 我的眼睛因困苦而干瘪。耶和华啊，我天天求告你，向你举手。
verses.en: My eyes grow weak because of oppression.I call out to you, O Lord, all day long;I spread out my hands in prayer to you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “[I am] confined and I cannot go out.”

verses.zh: 你岂要行奇事给死人看吗？难道阴魂还能起来称赞你吗？（细拉）
verses.en: Do you accomplish amazing things for the dead?Do the departed spirits[NOTE:1] rise up and give you thanks? (Selah)
notes: Heb “I spread out my hands to you.” Spreading out the hands toward God was a prayer gesture (see Exod 9:29, 33; 1 Kgs 8:22, 38; 2 Chr 6:12-13, 29; Ezra 9:15; Job 11:13; Isa 1:15). The words “in prayer” have been supplied in the translation to clarify this.

verses.zh: 岂能在坟墓里述说你的慈爱吗？岂能在灭亡中述说你的信实吗？
verses.en: Is your loyal love proclaimed in the grave,or your faithfulness in the place of the dead?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Rephaim,” a term that refers to those who occupy the land of the dead (see Isa 14:9; 26:14, 19).

verses.zh: 你的奇事岂能在幽暗里被知道吗？你的公义岂能在忘记之地被知道吗？
verses.en: Are your amazing deeds experienced[NOTE:1] in the dark region,[NOTE:2] or your deliverance in the land of oblivion?[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “in Abaddon,” a name for Sheol. The noun is derived from a verbal root meaning “to perish,” “to die.”
Heb “known.”
Heb “darkness,” here a title for Sheol.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我呼求你；我早晨的祷告要达到你面前。
verses.en: As for me, I cry out to you, O Lord;in the morning my prayer confronts you.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你为何丢弃我？为何掩面不顾我？
verses.en: O Lord, why do you reject me,and pay no attention to me?[NOTE:1]
notes: The rhetorical questions in vv. 10-12 expect the answer, “Of course not!”tn Heb “forgetfulness.” The noun, which occurs only here in the OT, is derived from a verbal root meaning “to forget.”

verses.zh: 我自幼受苦，几乎死亡；我受你的惊恐，甚至慌张。
verses.en: I am oppressed and have been on the verge of death since my youth.[NOTE:1] I have been subjected to your horrors and am numb with pain.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[why] do you hide your face from me?”
Heb “and am dying from youth.”

verses.zh: 你的烈怒漫过我身；你的惊吓把我剪除。
verses.en: Your anger overwhelms me;[NOTE:1] your terrors destroy me.
notes: Heb “I carry your horrors [?].” The meaning of the Hebrew form אָפוּנָה (ʾafunah), which occurs only here in the OT, is unclear. It may be an adverb meaning “very much” (BDB 67 s.v.), though some prefer to emend the text to אָפוּגָה (ʾafugah, “I am numb”) from the verb פוּג (pug; see Pss 38:8; 77:2).

verses.zh: 这些终日如水环绕我，一齐都来围困我。
verses.en: They surround me like water all day long;they join forces and encircle me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “passes over me.”

verses.zh: 你把我的良朋密友隔在远处，使我所认识的人进入黑暗里。
verses.en: You cause my friends and neighbors to keep their distance;[NOTE:1] those who know me leave me alone in the darkness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they encircle me together.”
Heb “you cause to be far from me friend and neighbor.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible
Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This Psalm has a long introduction in the MT. However, these superscriptions were not
part of the original Psalm. They are not present in the Dead Sea Scrolls. They are in the LXX.
Often they

- deal with musical issues, therefore, later developed temple worship liturgy

- are inaccurate historical allusions

For more information, see Introduction to the Psalms, IV and VII

- This Psalm is characterized by

- a series of questions related to the author's sense of rejection by God,
cf. Ps. 88:10-12,14. This Psalm ends with no hope or relief in sight! This is a "dark" Psalm!

- a series of titles/names for the afterlife

- Sheol, Ps. 88:3b ‒ BDB 982, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL

- the pit, Ps. 88:4a ‒ BDB 92 I

- among the dead, Ps. 88:5a ‒ BDB 559

- who lie in the grave, Ps. 88:5b ‒ BDB 868

- whom You remember no more, Ps. 88:5c

- cut off from Your hand, Ps. 88:5d, cf. Lam. 3:54

- the lowest pit, Ps. 88:6a ‒ BDB 1066

- dark places, Ps. 88:6b ‒ BDB 365

- the depths, Ps. 88:6b ‒ BDB 846 (g, h, i are parallel)

- the dead, Ps. 88:10a ‒ BDB 559

- the departed spirits, Ps. 88:10b ‒ BDB 952 I

- the grave, Ps. 88:11a ‒ BDB 868

- the place of destruction, Ps. 88:11b ‒ lit. abaddon - BDB 2

- the darkness, Ps. 88:12a ‒ BDB 365, cf. 1 Sam. 2:9; Job 10:21; 17:13; 18:18

- the land of forgetfulness, Ps. 88:12b ‒ BDB 75 CONSTRUCT
BDB 674 (unique to this Psalm, cf. Ps. 6:5)

- darkness, Ps. 88:18b ‒ BDB 365

- Notice the different words used to describe God's rejection.

- Your wrath, Ps. 88:7a ‒ BDB 404

- Your waves, Ps. 88:7b ‒ BDB 991, cf. Ps. 42:7; 69:1,14-15; Jonah 2:3

- You reject, Ps. 88:14a ‒ VERB, BDB 276 I, KB 276,
Qal IMPERFECT

- You hide Your face, Ps. 88:14b ‒ VERB,
BDB 711, KB 771, Hiphil IMPERFECT

- Your terrors, Ps. 88:15b ‒ BDB 33

- Your burning anger, Ps. 88:16a ‒ BDB 354

- Your terrors, Ps. 88:16b ‒ BDB 130 (only here and Job 6:4)

- It is hard from this brief Psalm to know if the psalmist is

- sick (possibly leprosy because of his abandonment by family and friends)

- suffering from divine judgment

- feeling a sense of being alone (depression)

- fearful of life's circumstances

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 88:1-9

1O
Lord, the God of my salvation,

I have cried out by day and in
the night before You.

2Let my prayer come
before You;

Incline Your ear to my cry!

3For my soul has had
enough troubles,

And my life has drawn near to
Sheol.

4I am reckoned among
those who go down to the pit;

I have become like a man
without strength,

5Forsaken among the
dead,

Like the slain who lie in the
grave,

Whom You remember no more,

And they are cut off from Your
hand.

6You have put me in
the lowest pit,

In dark places, in the depths.

7Your wrath has
rested upon me,

And You have afflicted me with
all Your waves.
Selah.

8You have removed my
acquaintances far from me;

You have made me an object of
loathing to them;

I am shut up and cannot go out.

9My eye has wasted
away because of affliction;

I have called upon You every

I have spread out my hands to

88:1 "O Lord" This Psalm
uses the covenant name for Deity, YHWH, in a VOCATIVE sense
three times. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "the God of my salvation" This title
for Deity (cf. Ps. 24:5; 27:9) is descriptive of what the psalmist wants YHWH to
do for him, "save," "deliver," "act on his behalf." This opening verse is the
most "positive" line of the Psalm. YHWH is the Covenant God and the psalmist
prays but senses no response. He even feels God has purposefully caused his
plight!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

▣ "I" Notice the number of FIRST PERSON SINGULAR PRONOUNS
and SECOND PERSON SINGULAR PRONOUNS ("You"). This is
a very personal cry from a believer to his God.

▣ "I have cried out" This VERB (BDB 858,
KB 1042) is the first of many PERFECT VERBS. The psalmist is asserting his
diligent seeking of God but God has not yet responded (cf. Ps. 88:13-18).

▣ "by day and in the night" This
phrase is the psalmist's way of asserting his constant prayer (cf. Ps. 22:2;
25:5; 86:3).

88:2 This verse has two parallel requests.

- let my prayer come before You ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense (cf. Ps. 18:6); the psalmist felt his prayer was not
being heard (cf. Ps. 88:9,13,14)

- incline Your ear to my cry ‒ BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
(cf. Ps. 17:6; 31:2; 71:2; 86:1; 102:2)

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMOPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

88:3-9 The psalmist lists the reasons why God should hear and respond (the
PERFECT describes a settled condition).

- his soul (BDB 659) is full (another PERFECT) of troubles, Ps. 88:3a; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

- his life (BDB 313) has arrived (another PERFECT) near to Sheol
(see
SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?), Ps. 88:3b

- he is reckoned (another PERFECT) among those who go down to
the pit (cf. Ps. 28:1; 143:7), Ps. 88:4a

- he has become (another PERFECT) like a man without strength
(i.e., helpless, BDB 33, only here in the OT; Aramaic loan word), Ps. 88:4b

- he has been forsaken "among the dead"; the ADJECTIVE translated
"forsaken" is lit. "freed," BDB 344, Ps. 88:5a

- NKJV "adrift"

- TEV, JPSOA "abandoned"

- NJB "left alone"

The MT has "freed" and seems to refer to the freedom from all the
responsibilities of life (cf. USB Text Project, p. 350).

- he whom You remember (another PERFECT) no more, Ps. 88:5c

- he whom You cut off (another PERFECT) from Your hand, Ps. 88:5d; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

- he whom You have put (another PERFECT) in the lowest pit, Ps. 88:6a

- he whom You have put in dark places, in the depths, Ps. 88:6b

- he on whom Your wrath has rested (lit. "lies heavy," another PERFECT)
Ps. 88:7a (this VERB BDB 701, KB 759 is mostly used of YHWH
upporting someone but here, the antithesis)

- he whom You have afflicted (lit. "overwhelmed," another PERFECT)
with all Your waves, Ps. 88:7b

- he whom You have removed his acquaintances far away (another PERFECT), Ps. 88:8a

- he whom You have made an object of loathing (another PERFECT), Ps. 88:8b

- he whom You have shut up, Ps. 88:8c

- his eyes have wasted away (another PERFECT), Ps. 88:9a

- he has called upon You every day (another PERFECT), cf. Ps. 88:1b, 9b

- he has spread out his hands (i.e., prayer, another PERFECT) to You, Ps. 88:9c

Notice the combination of

- the psalmist's acts

- the things he asserts that God has done to him

The MT has the ADJECTIVE "free" (BDB 344, KB 341), possibly meaning

- cut off from YHWH's remembrances by death

- relieved of all responsibilities of this life by death

- he felt abandoned by YHWH in life and now in death

88:7 "all Your waves" This is referring to ocean waves (BDB 991).

- literally ‒ Jonah 2:3

- figuratively of calamities ‒ Ps. 32:6; 42:7; 69:1-2

Water imagery was powerful to desert peoples! This psalmist thought all his problems
were sent by his covenant God. Apparently he does not know why. He mentions no acts of sin or unbelief.

88:7 "Selah" See notes at Psalm 3:2.

88:8 "acquaintances" This (BDB 393, KB 390) is a Pual PARTICIPLE
from the VERB "to know" (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW).
The same form is also in Ps. 88:18 along with

- lover ‒ BDB 12, KB 17 Qal PARTICIPLE

- friend ‒ BDB 945

This man felt totally alienated from God and other humans!

88:9 Psalm 88:9 is similar in content to Ps. 88:1 and may be an example of inclusio.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 88:10-12

10Will You perform
wonders for the dead?

Will the departed spirits rise
and praise You?
Selah.

11Will Your lovingkindness be
declared in the grave,

Your faithfulness in Abaddon?

12Will Your wonders
be made known in the darkness?

And Your righteousness in the
land of forgetfulness?

88:10-12 This strophe describes the general OT view of the joyless, silent
existence of the conscious soul/person/self in the afterlife.

- God did not deliver ("save") from the dead

- the dead do not praise God (cf. Ps. 6:5; 30:9; 115:17; Isa. 38:18)

- God's faithfulness is not declared in the grave (cf. Isa. 38:18)

- God's acts of deliverance (BDB 810, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS) are not declared in the darkness

- God's righteousness (i.e., His acts of salvation) is not declared in the land of forgetfulness

Because of Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28 it is possible to see these as departed

13But I, O Lord, have cried out to You for help,

And in the morning my prayer
comes before You.

14O
Lord, why do You reject my soul?

Why do You hide Your
face from me?

15I was afflicted
and about to die from my youth on;

I suffer Your terrors; I am

88:13-18 This repeats the emphasis of
the previous verses. The psalmist feels estranged from God and family and
friends (cf. v. 18)! He is alone! This Psalm ends in despair (cf. Ps. 88:14)! He does not
understand what is happening to him, either physically or spiritually!

88:15 Does this verse imply that the
psalmist has been sick from his youth and is near death or is this imagery of a
prolonged sense of abandonment by God?

The VERB in the MT (BDB 806, KB 918, Qal
IMPERFECT) can be from one of three roots.

- אפונה ‒ BDB 67, either

- "to be helpless"

- to be confused"

- "very, very much"

- פון ‒ found only here and meaning uncertain

- פוג ‒ "to grow numb" (NET Bible)

This verse is difficult to translate because the MT is difficult (JPSOA footnote)

88:18 "in darkness" The same
consonants can mean "withholding" (Peshitta). JPSOA takes the MT "darkness" and
translates it as "cannot see."

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide
commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of
the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the
Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a
commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think
through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought provoking, not definitive.

- As you read this Psalm what is your first impression?

- What is the psalmist's problem?

- Why does he feel God has abandoned him? Does he express any hope? How?

- Describe the OT view of the afterlife.

- Why is Ps. 88:4 so painful?

- Does the psalmist express any hope that God will hear, come, help?
